summary: Exact split (scripts/z52d_p2_SK1_semiprime.py): solutions of 4/(pq) with all denominators divisible by q (resp. p) are the scaled solutions of 4/p (resp. 4/q), and the two families are disjoint, so inherited = U(p)+U(q) exactly; over all 5706 odd semiprimes pq<=3e4 the non-inherited part is U(pq)-U(p)-U(q) >= 4 always, median 88% of U(pq), and log(new) ~ 0.19 log U(p) (smaller factor) with no dependence on U(q).

next: Characterise the non-inherited solutions (e.g. by which denominators are divisible by p or q) to see if they come from a second scaling lemma.

summary: Exact: U(p)-D(p) = 2 for every odd prime p=3 mod 4 and 0 for p=1 mod 4 (no p>7 restriction needed). Proof: non-distinct solutions are multisets {u,u,v} with u!=v, i.e. pairs (u,v) with 2/u+1/v=4/p; by the factorisation lemma (fingerprint-0229) there are exactly two such pairs iff p=3 mod 4, both with u!=v: (u,v)=((p+1)/2, p(p+1)/4) and (p(p+1)/2, (p+1)/4). Checked numerically for all 3244 primes 3<=p<=3e4 (scripts/z52d_p2_SK1_isosceles.py, data/z52b/pass2/SK1/Z0833_count4_all_3e4.txt). Consequence: the ordered count O = 6D + 3(U-D) + 0 gives O = 6U-6 at p=3 mod 4 and O = 6U at p=1 mod 4 (all-equal triples are impossible for p>2), so the orbit formula of fingerprint-0266 also follows.
not_done: Orbit formula checked against A292624 data only implicitly (not fetched).
next: Confirm A292624 (= O(p)) matches 6U-6 / 6U at all primes in the OEIS b-file.
